newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists split on short-term AEX.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists split on short-term AEX.

text.p: Dutch chartists were divided on the immediate prospects for the AEX index, with some predicting a hesitation or even reversal of the short-term uptrend while others maintained a bullish outlook.
ING Barings said the short-term uptrend lacked conviction, while MeesPierson forecast a small fall in the index towards short-term support at 742.
However ABN AMRO said the AEX's success in holding up above 780 points should be seen in a positive light and predicted further rises after short-term consolidation.
RABO, too, said the uptrend remained intact.

The AEX share index closed at 780.81 last Friday, back slightly from last Tuesday's all-time high of 786.82. The index started Monday a touch higher at 783.42 but volumes were slight. Contributor Trend Pvs view Support Resistance

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.

ING Barings -- The short term uptrend of the Amsterdam stock market is still intact, however lacks conviction. Last week's string of new all-time highs of the AEX has not been confirmed by a surge in trading volume, suggesting an absence of immediate buying interest. It also reveals that there is a lot of liquidity on the sidelines still waiting to pour into the market. Another negative is a lagging Advance/Decline line, which signals that there is no leadership in the market. History shows that major bull markets never start without strong leadership. As momentum is already fading away, the internal technicals of the AEX are slowly eroding.

(ING Barings continued.) A close below MA9 at 770 would violate the rising trend channel, signalling a deeper correction towards 749. Then next support comes in around 740. However it could be rewarding to buy the dips in the 740-750 range, as long-term technicals of the AEX remain solid and sound.

MeesPierson -- The short-term technical outlook for the AEX remains limited. In the previous week the index barely moved from its place, so we are now ready to take a (little) dive in the direction of the short-term support level of 742.
Furthermore the dollar chart indicates a further decline to the level of 1.86-1.87, where there is short-term support.
RABO Securities -- The uptrend remains intact as well as our first price target at 790. The positive outlook will be damaged somehow on a break of 767.

ABN AMRO -- After the corrective move within the last week, the AEX has succeeded in sustaining stability above the 780 level. Given that last week comprised some days during which a number of stocks paid their dividends, the ability to remain stable around these levels must be seen in a positive light.
At the beginning of this week we see no warnings on the RSI, indicating a low-risk situation.
(ABN AMRO continued.) In other words, we are still focused on the 800 level within the near future after the short-term consolidation around present levels has passed.

However, an exit-stop level at 775 is advised to stay on the safe side. Even in the scenario that these price levels become reality, the medium term direction remains strongly up. So focus up, don't even think about short term SHORT strategies, the risk remains on the upside!!
